column7: suspending a machine identity took effect only on the replica that ran it: CurrentMachineTokenRestriction returned a non-active owning identity as a bare fmt.Errorf which serveAuthCacheHit cannot distinguish from a storage blip, so the cache-hit path took the degrade-to-stale branch and the token kept authenticating for up to validTokenTTL (30s) on every other replica. Now core.ErrMachineIdentityNotActive, denied alongside the revoked/expired sentinels; the previously t.Skip-ped test is un-skipped in the same change

core half of mi-suspend-cachehit-001: every non-active machine identity state yields core.ErrMachineIdentityNotActive (errors.Is, not a message match), with both calibration directions - an active identity still succeeds, and a transient storage failure is NOT reported as the sentinel so a blip cannot start denying on the cache-hit path
